A bar tack now sits at the corner. All three of the prior errors (geometry / construction / angles) are resolved.

REMAINING BLOCKER - one major, in dimensions. The vertical drop from the waistband seam to the corner is 0.612 waistband-depths where the drawing gives 0.744-0.831. That is 18-26 percent short. Waistband depth was validated as a landmark before use (drawing 103.5 px across five columns, render 131.5 px across two), and because both the drop and the normaliser are vertical, this shortfall survives the perspective correction that explains away every other size difference. Fixing it means moving the corner down roughly 23 px in this render's scale and nothing else.

WHAT I CHECKED THAT TURNED OUT NOT TO BE AN ERROR. My first pass read the run as 43 percent short (1.88 waistband-depths vs 3.29 drawn) and the corner as 11 degrees too steep. Both collapsed under normalisation. Three independent horizontal landmarks - belt-loop pitch, welt length, and the crease's own position - all compress by the same 0.60-0.66 factor in the render relative to the drawing, so the run's apparent shortfall is this camera's foreshortening, not a pocket error; the arm sits only 0.025 belt-loop-pitches (about 11 px) inboard of drawn. Likewise, the raw 11.4 degree run-inclination gap falls to 3.6 degrees once measured against each image's own waistband bottom seam. I am flagging this explicitly because a regeneration that "fixes" the run length would break a geometry that is currently correct.

MEASUREMENTS I COULD NOT MAKE. (1) No centimetre figures are recoverable. The tech pack carries no printed dimension callout, so every number above is a ratio against a shared landmark; the spec's "90 degrees" is a label, not a drawing callout. (2) The drawing itself measures 96.5 degrees at the corner, not 90 - the label overstates squareness by 6.5 degrees, and I graded against the drawing. (3) I could not confirm whether the mouth carries visible topstitching. The luminance profile 9 px below the slot shows a ~6.1 px periodicity, but the twill's own diagonal gives a control residual of 10.9 std against the lip's 15.0, which is not enough separation to call it. The drawing shows a plain line with no stitch marks, so nothing is demanded either way.
